title: Stakeholder coordination
audience: Supervisors who coordinate cleaning work with building managers, clients and other site staff.
learningOutcomes: Identify the stakeholders for a site and what each needs to know.
Use one agreed communication channel for schedules, changes and issues.
Record decisions and send confirmations to the right people.

instruction.heading: Who needs to know
instruction.body: A cleaning site has several stakeholders, and each needs different information. The building manager or client needs the schedule, the changes, the access arrangements and any incident. The site staff need the zones that will be worked, the times when areas are occupied, and any restriction on entry. Other contractors need to know the times they share with you, the areas they will use, and any isolation or delivery that affects the route. Occupants need to know when their area will be disturbed and how to raise a concern. Your supervisor needs every request that falls outside the agreement, every issue that is not resolved on site, and every change that affects the team. Emergency contacts for the site are held on the site schedule. For each site, list the stakeholders, the information each one needs, how often they need it, and the channel through which it reaches them. A one-page table is enough for most sites, and it should be checked when the site changes.

instruction.heading: One agreed channel
instruction.body: Use one agreed channel for schedules, changes and issues at each site. The channel might be a shared email thread, a messaging group, a logbook at reception or a ticketing system, but it must be agreed with the client and written into the site arrangement. Mixing channels is a common cause of lost information. A change sent by text to one person, an email to another and a remark in a corridor will not reach everyone who needs it. Keep each message brief, dated and factual: what changes, when it takes effect, who is affected, and why. A change that is given verbally is not a recorded change until it is confirmed in the channel. Ask the person who gave the change to confirm it in the channel, or send the confirmation yourself and ask them to reply.

instruction.heading: Confirmations and disputes
instruction.body: Send confirmations of schedule changes, access arrangements and reported issues to the people who need them, and keep a copy. A confirmation should state the change, the time it takes effect, the reason, the area affected, the person who approved it, and the people it has been sent to. When a stakeholder asks for something outside the agreement, refer it to the supervisor rather than agreeing it at the door. Describe an issue in facts: what you saw, where, when, and who was told. Do not speculate about cause or blame, and do not promise a fix. If a dispute arises over what was agreed, the channel record and the confirmations are the first reference, followed by the contract and any variation (see “Site contract and scope”).

instruction.heading: Handling a difficult conversation
instruction.body: Some stakeholders will be unhappy about a delay, a noise, or a change they did not expect. Listen to the concern, repeat it back in plain words so that the person knows it has been heard, and say what you will do next. Do not promise a change you cannot make. Record the concern in the channel, and pass it to the supervisor if it needs a decision. Keep your tone calm and factual. A short, accurate message in the channel protects the relationship better than a long conversation at the door that nobody else can see.

procedure: List the stakeholders for each site, what each needs to know, how often, and the channel that reaches them.
Use the agreed channel for schedules, changes and issues, and do not split information across channels.
Confirm any verbal change in the channel with the time, the reason, the area and the approver, and keep a record.
Send confirmations to the right people and keep copies.
Refer any request outside the agreement to the supervisor, and record the concern before the conversation ends.

workedExamples.situation: A site staff member changes the cleaning time verbally in a corridor, so that the cleaning now starts an hour earlier.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not simply accept it and move on. Confirm the change in the agreed channel with the new time, the reason and the areas affected, and ask the staff member to confirm it in reply. Tell the supervisor and the team, so that the change is known to everyone who works the site. Keep the record. If the earlier start affects access or other contractors, check it with the building manager before it takes effect.

workedExamples.situation: A contractor asks for the service corridor to be closed for an hour while they unload stock.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Who must agree, and how is it recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not agree at the door. Refer the request to the supervisor, who checks it with the building manager through the agreed channel. Once the closure is approved, confirm it in the channel with the time, the area and the approver, and tell the cleaning team. If the cleaning cannot be done during the closure, note the affected area in the handover, so that the work is not lost.

workedExamples.situation: An occupant complains in writing that the cleaning noise disturbed an important meeting in an adjacent room.
workedExamples.reasoning: Acknowledge the complaint in the channel, and record its time, location and the detail the occupant gives. Do not argue about whether the noise was necessary. Pass the complaint to the supervisor, who decides whether the timing or the method changes at that site. Confirm the next step to the occupant through the channel, and do not promise a result before the decision is made.

equipmentAndPpe: Agreed communication channel for the site, as written into the site arrangement.
Stakeholder list for each site, with the information needs and the channel for each.
Issue report form, and the supervisor's contact details as the business provides them.
No PPE is set by this lesson. Site PPE applies when you are on the site.

commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the change in the agreed channel, and ask for a reply.

commonErrors.error: Telling only one stakeholder about a change.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the stakeholder list, and inform everyone who needs the change.

commonErrors.error: Agreeing an out-of-scope request at the door.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the request to the supervisor, and tell the requester that it is being checked.

commonErrors.error: Splitting information across text, email and corridor conversations.
commonErrors.prevention: Use one channel, and move any verbal information into it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson does not state a regulatory requirement for stakeholder communication. The channel, reporting route and escalation contacts come from the contract and the site arrangement.

Confidential information shared through the channel: do not post personal or client information in a group channel where people outside the need-to-know list can see it. Follow the site privacy procedure, as set out in the access lesson (“Office access, keys, alarms and confidentiality”).

qualityStandard: Stakeholders listed for a sample site, each with what they need to know and the channel that reaches them.
Verbal change confirmed in the agreed channel in the role-play, with the time, reason, area and approver.
Out-of-scope request referred to the supervisor, and not agreed at the door, in the case study.
No personal or client information shared outside the need-to-know list.
documentationEvidence: Stakeholder list and channel record for each site.
Confirmation copies for schedule changes, access arrangements and issues.
Issue or complaint log showing the time, the detail given and the decision.
summary: List each site's stakeholders and what each one needs to know.
Use one agreed channel, and confirm every change in it.
Refer out-of-scope requests to the supervisor and do not agree them at the door.
Record concerns in facts, and keep copies of every confirmation.

knowledgeChecks.question: A staff member changes the time verbally. What is correct?
options: Accept it and say nothing, since the change is small and easy
Confirm it in the agreed channel with the time and the reason
Ignore it until the next scheduled review of the roster

knowledgeChecks.question: Why use one channel?
options: It is cheaper to run than several channels
It keeps schedules, changes and issues traceable
It is required by a regulator in every state

knowledgeChecks.question: A request is outside the agreement. What is correct?
options: Agree it at the door to keep the client happy with the service
Refer it to the supervisor, and do not agree it at the door
Do it quickly and tell no one about the request at all

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the building manager or client need, according to the lesson?
options: The schedule, the changes, the access arrangements and any incident
